form_name: Form 6900 (Alaska Partnership Information Return)
filer: Partnerships/LLCs taxed as partnerships with a corporate or partnership partner and nexus in Alaska; S corporations doing business in Alaska file Form 6000 (see note)
rule: Alaska requires a partnership (or LLC taxed as a partnership) with nexus in Alaska to file Form 6900 only if at least one partner/member is a corporation or another partnership (a partnership whose partners are all natural persons is not required to file). The Alaska partnership return is due 30 days after the federal partnership return's due date (not the same calendar date each year, since it tracks the federal due date including any weekend/holiday shift) - for the 2025 tax year, 30 days after the federal 1065 due date of March 16, 2026, is April 15, 2026. Separately, an S corporation doing business in Alaska must file Form 6000 (the same corporate income tax return C corporations use), but Alaska does not tax the S corporation on its pass-through income; most S corporations satisfy the filing obligation by completing only page 1 and checking the S Corporation box, unless the corporate-level built-in-gains or excess-net-passive-income tax applies.
extension_form: A federal extension (Form 7004) automatically extends the Alaska Form 6900 due date to 30 days after the federal extended due date; attach a copy of the federal extension.
description: Alaska Form 6900 (Partnership Information Return) is due 30 days after the federal partnership return's due date - April 15, 2026 for the 2025 tax year (30 days after the federal 1065 due date of March 16, 2026) - and is required only when at least one partner is a corporation or another partnership; a partnership with only natural-person partners has no Alaska filing requirement. A federal extension automatically extends the Alaska due date to 30 days after the federal extended due date (October 15, 2026). S corporations doing business in Alaska separately file Form 6000 (the corporate return), though Alaska generally does not tax S corporations on pass-through income.
authority: Alaska Department of Revenue, Instructions for Form 6900 (Alaska Partnership Information Return): "A partnership or an LLC treated as a partnership for tax purposes ... which conducts business in the state (also known as having 'nexus' with the state) is required to file Form 6900. If all of the partners or LLC members ... are natural persons or are effectively treated as natural persons, the partnership is not required to file Form 6900." "The Alaska partnership return must be filed within 30 days of the date on which the partnership's federal return is required to be filed." "A federal extension automatically extends the Alaska filing due date to 30 days after the federal extended due date." S-corp treatment per Instructions for Form 6000: "An S Corporation doing business in Alaska is required to file an Alaska return, but Alaska does not impose a tax on the S Corporation for pass-through items of income," subject to the built-in-gains and excess-net-passive-income exceptions. rule: DC's partnership return (D-65) and unincorporated business franchise tax return (D-30) are both confirmed due April 15, 2026 for a calendar-year filer, directly from the current (2025 tax year) OTR booklets for each form. DC does not recognize federal S-corp status for franchise tax purposes - S corporations doing business in DC generally file the D-20 corporate return instead, not D-65 or D-30.
